name: 157. Extended output batches, logprobs and batch create pins (batch and logprobs pins)
description: Closes rows that docs research turned from held into buildable. output-300k-2026-03-24 is a real Message Batches beta: it raises max_tokens to 300,000 on Opus 4.7/4.8/5(.5) and Sonnet 4.6/5(.5), is not available on the synchronous Messages API, Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry, and output-128k is retired (docs: platform.claude.com batch-processing). 157.1a/b create a batch with max_tokens 200000 and cancel it immediately; they are [PREVIEW] because the beta needs org access, and 157.1a/b share h157BatchId. Gemini response logprobs: 157.2 is an [EXPECT-4XX] out-of-range pin that proves the field reaches Google; 157.3 is the [PREVIEW] positive case because model support could not be confirmed from the docs. Azure batch create (157.4a/b, [PREVIEW]) needs a Global Batch deployment named by azureBatchDeployment and shares h157AzureBatchId.

item.name: 157.1a [PREVIEW] anthropic message batch with output-300k-2026-03-24 accepts max_tokens above the 128k standard cap (extended output batch)

exec: pm.test('batch accepted with the extended-output beta header', function () { pm.expect(j.type, pm.response.text()).to.equal('message_batch'); pm.expect(j.id, pm.response.text()).to.match(/^msgbatch_/); pm.expect(['in_progress', 'canceling', 'ended'], pm.response.text()).to.include(j.processing_status); });

item.name: 157.1b [PREVIEW] anthropic message batch cancel stops the extended-output batch before it bills output (extended output batch)

exec: pm.test('cancel accepted for the created batch', function () { pm.expect(j.id, pm.response.text()).to.equal(pm.collectionVariables.get('h157BatchId')); pm.expect(['canceling', 'ended'], pm.response.text()).to.include(j.processing_status); });

item.name: 157.2 [EXPECT-4XX] gemini-2.5-flash native logprobs above the allowed range reaches Google (response logprobs)

exec: pm.test('Google names the logprobs setting in its rejection', function () { var t = pm.response.text(); pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'expected Google’s 400 validation error: ' + t).to.equal(400); pm.expect(t, 'an authentication error proves nothing about the parameter: ' + t).to.not.match(/API key|API_KEY_INVALID|UNAUTHENTICATED|PERMISSION_DENIED|authentication credentials/i); pm.expect(t, 'rejection does not name the logprobs/range; field may not have reached Google: ' + t).to.match(/logprob/i); });

item.name: 157.3 [PREVIEW] gemini-2.5-flash native responseLogprobs returns logprobsResult with top candidates (response logprobs)

exec: pm.test('candidate carries logprobsResult with top candidates', function () { pm.expect(cand.logprobsResult, 'no logprobsResult (model may not support logprobs): ' + pm.response.text().slice(0, 600)).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect((cand.logprobsResult.topCandidates || []).length, pm.response.text().slice(0, 600)).to.be.above(0); });

item.name: 157.2b [EXPECT-4XX] gemini-2.5-flash pinned to its provider keeps logprobs on the raw path, so Google rejects a value above the allowed range (response logprobs)

exec: pm.test('Google rejects the out-of-range logprobs with a 4xx', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'want a 4xx from Google (a 200 means logprobs were stripped before the call): ' + pm.response.text().slice(0, 600)).to.be.within(400, 499); });
pm.test('the rejection names logprobs', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text(), 'rejection does not mention logprobs: ' + pm.response.text().slice(0, 600)).to.match(/logprob/i); });
pm.test('no other provider answered', function () { if (served) { pm.expect(served, 'served by another provider: ' + pm.response.text().slice(0, 400)).to.equal('gemini'); } });
